messages:
Alex M: quick sync — SRE asked for a short proposal on how we should treat per-API-key limits vs org-level quotas for internal services and partner integrations. partner wants sustained high qps for a pilot. thoughts?

Jamie L: which partner and what kind of sustained qps? are they asking to bypass org caps or just a higher key-level cap?

Alex M: partner=EdgeMaps (mapping tile gen). pilot peak ~1000 qps sustained for 3h/day, normal <200. they want deterministic latency; billing will still be on their org but they asked us to allow a per-key override to avoid cascading throttles.

Sara P: we currently enforce per-org and per-key concurrently: effective limit = min(org_cap, key_cap). the problem is we have a manual "override" flow that sets a key_cap > org_cap in the DB for special keys — that effectively nullifies org protections if not guarded. risky.

Matt R: +1. proposal: introduce TTL'ed key-level tiers (pilot, prod, emergency) and add a routing-level circuit breaker that honors a separate burst budget. so key_cap can exceed org_cap only in a controlled, audited way.

Sara P: rough config sketch I mocked for the API server:
```yaml
key_overrides:
  partner-edgemaps-prod:
    tier: pilot
    qps: 1200
    burst_tokens: 6000 # allow short bursts above steady qps
    ttl: 90d
    approved_by: "platform-oncall"
    audit_note: "pilot - edgemaps tiles - expires"
```

Jamie L: nice. question: how do we prevent cost/accounting surprises? if key_cap > org_cap we need a billing guardrail: alert if monthly spend projection delta > X% and auto-revoke if >Y.

Alex M: agree. for billing/console UX we should show a warning badge on the org page when any key has an override. also require a documented justification and a billing contact.

Matt R: telemetry needs: per-key token spend, per-key latency p50/p95, and burst_token consumption meter. also backfill into tracing so we can see which route served the extra traffic. alerts on sustained burst consumption > 10% for > 1hr.

Sara P: operationally we should make overrides require two actions: a platform engineer grant + a separate billing ack. single-click in console is too lax. UI: Approve override -> choose tier -> set TTL -> add justification -> require billing checkbox. we store the approval as immutable audit event.

Jamie L: routing implications: if a key is given higher qps we should route to dedicated pools or higher-priority nodes (dedicated or dedicated-shared). otherwise regular pools will starve. set a routing policy field: route_policy: dedicated|standard|fallback.

Alex M: fallback policy must include automatic model downgrade or fallback to lower-cost variants when capacity is constrained. this protects other customers. i.e., key_override = soft promise, not absolute SLA unless explicit contract.

quota-bot: [system] detected spike: partner-edgemaps-prod used 4.1M tokens in last 10m, burst budget remaining 1.2M.

Sara P: that bot alert is useful — makes the case for auto-revoke thresholds. also we should rate-limit the override API itself to avoid runaway automation.

Matt R: implementation notes: minimal server changes — add override table with state machine (requested -> approved -> active -> expired -> revoked). runtime checks: calculate effective_qps = base_key_qps + burst_window_allowance, but also check org_hard_cap unless approved_by_billing.

Alex M: action items: 1) Jamie to write the RFC for keys-as-tiers (include console UX mockups & billing guardrails) 2) Sara to spec telemetry & quota-bot alerts 3) Matt to prototype state machine + routing flag 4) I will coordinate with legal for any partner SLA language.

Jamie L: I'll kick off the RFC today, link in #eng-announce when ready.

Sara P: created GH issue PLATFORM-1189 to track; assigned to Matt + Jamie.

Matt R: will start a spike tomorrow to validate burst_token accounting under load.

Alex M: cool — thanks team. keep the console UX conservative: require explicit approvals and clear audit history. :thumbsup:
